messages.text: 'Like a mini World Cup' - Jacks sees positives in England's tri-series troubles

metadata.summary: Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory.
metadata.content: Will Jacks: England in 'mini World Cup' scenario as they enter must-win territory in tri-series with Pakistan and Sri Lanka | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Will Jacks: England in 'mini World Cup' scenario as they enter must-win territory in tri-series with Pakistan and Sri Lanka England followed an opening loss to Pakistan with a shock defeat to Sri Lanka despite a record-breaking 202 from Harry Brook; watch England's next tri-series match, against Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am, Sunday (8am first ball) Friday 23 October 2026 23:25, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook rewrites the record books, becoming the fastest player to reach an ODI double century before finishing on 202, the highest individual score ever recorded by an England batter in the format. Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory. England had looked set to bounce back from an 87-run hammering by Pakistan as Harry Brook's record-breaking 202 saw Sri Lanka set a massive 430 to win their match on Thursday, only for them to pull off a remarkable run chase on the penultimate ball. The two-wicket defeat means England arrive in Lahore knowing they must beat both Pakistan on Sunday and then Sri Lanka on Thursday to give themselves a chance of of reaching the final on Saturday, October 31. metadata.summary: Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.
metadata.content: Adrian Newey responds to Christian Horner's criticism of him in new book over Red Bull's struggles with Renault in 2014 | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Adrian Newey responds to Christian Horner's criticism of him in new book over Red Bull's struggles with Renault in 2014 In his autobiography, ex-Red Bull boss Christian Horner claims Adrian Newey" wanted to abandon ship" at "first sign of adversity" at team in 2014; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 24 October 2026 08:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Adrian Newey addressed Christian Horner's criticism made in his latest memoirs. Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book. Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024. But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014. messages.text: 'A clear red' - Should Ipswich's Diop have been sent off?

metadata.summary: Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not?
metadata.content: Ipswich's Issa Diop escaped a red card for a foul on Nottingham Forest's James McAtee - but was it the right call? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Ipswich's Issa Diop escaped a red card for a foul on Nottingham Forest's James McAtee - but was it the right call? Ipswich's Issa Diop was shown a yellow card for a last-man foul on James McAtee when it was deemed he didn't deny an obvious goal-scoring opportunity by referee Thomas Bramall after a VAR intervention; Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner said it was a 'clear red card' after the 1-1 draw Friday 23 October 2026 23:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Should Issa Diop have seen red for his challenge on James McAtee that he only got a yellow card for? Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not? With less than five minutes of the second half played when Diop slid in on Forest's James McAtee, a sending off could have transformed the outcome of the game. Glasner was adamant Diop had denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity. But Diop himself told Sky Sports he was "quite confident" he would stay on the field as the officials and VAR came to their decision. There was also split opinion among the Sky Sports pundits, too. messages.text: Dubois on the lesson of Fury-AJ: 'I want to fight Itauma sooner'

metadata.summary: Daniel Dubois believes he and Moses Itauma must learn a lesson from Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua – if they are to fight, they need to do it sooner rather than later.
metadata.content: Daniel Dubois on the lesson of Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua for him and Moses Itauma: 'I want to fight him sooner' | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Daniel Dubois on the lesson of Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua for him and Moses Itauma: 'I want to fight him sooner' Daniel Dubois believes there is a lesson for himself and Moses Itauma to learn from Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua - don't wait too long to fight; Dubois is convinced he's the hardest puncher in world but warns he's getting even more powerful: "I'm just starting to unload properly now" John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Thursday 22 October 2026 22:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player WBO heavyweight world champion Daniel Dubois says he is eyeing a future clash against Tyson Fury next year, admitting the fight would be 'ground-breaking'. Daniel Dubois believes he and Moses Itauma must learn a lesson from Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua – if they are to fight, they need to do it sooner rather than later. Fury and Joshua have been British heavyweight rivals for almost a decade but missed the chance to fight each other at the peak of their careers, though they will now finally box in December. A major rivalry for the next generation of British heavyweight boxers could develop between Dubois and Moses Itauma. metadata.content: United States GP: Charles Leclerc edges Kimi Antonelli in Practice Two to complete Friday double for Ferrari | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content United States GP: Charles Leclerc edges Kimi Antonelli in Practice Two to complete Friday double for Ferrari Charles Leclerc tops both Friday practice sessions in Austin; Ferrari driver edged out Kimi Antonelli in second practice; watch every United States GP session live on Sky Sports F1, with qualifying at 10pm on Saturday and the race at 8pm on Sunday Saturday 24 October 2026 07:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the United States Grand Prix. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc edged out Kimi Antonelli to complete a Friday practice double at the United States Grand Prix. After narrowly topping Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the opening session, Leclerc improved by almost eight tenths of a second later in the day to finish 0.042s clear of Mercedes' Antonelli, who could become Formula 1's youngest ever world champion on Sunday. Verstappen appears to be in contention to extend his streak of two successive victories after finishing the second session in third, within a couple of tenths of Leclerc's leading time of 1:35.291s. metadata.content: Katie Boulter loses to Katerina Siniakova in straight sets in semi-finals of Japan Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Katie Boulter loses to Katerina Siniakova in straight sets in semi-finals of Japan Open Katerina Siniakova beat Katie Boulter 6-1 6-4 in the semi-finals of the Japan Open in Osaka; watch the WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports , with this week's action including events in China, Japan, Kazakhstan, France and Belgium Saturday 24 October 2026 12:25, UK Image: Boulter's form has seen her reclaim the British No 1 ranking Katie Boulter lost to Katerina Siniakova in the semi-finals of the Japan Open on Saturday. Siniakova won in straight sets, 6-1 6-4. Boulter had reached her third WTA semi-final of the 2026 season and she has reclaimed her place as British No 1. Tennis scores, results and schedule from around the world Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news, video and more But her run came to an end in Osaka with Siniakova starting their semi-final match up strongly. The Czech won the first five games of the match and Boulter had to save a set point to win her first game. Boulter stirred hopes of a fightback when she broke Siniakova but the Czech soon seized back control. The Briton showed greater resistance in the second set but Siniakova served out for a straightforward victory. Siniakova, the world No 86, will face the USA's Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final. Katsuragawa shot a flawless eight-under 63 in the third round at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club, including four birdies in his first five holes, to match Jinam Kang's record in 2006. The 28-year-old Katsuragawa is 13 under overall, two shots ahead of South Africa's Casey Jarvis.
